text:
evan.m: Morning — weird COB problem. Had a specialist visit on 2026-03-22. EOBs show my spouse's employer plan paid primary and Redwood paid secondary, but I confirmed with my spouse that their plan should've been secondary (they're a dependent under my plan). How do we get this corrected?

sophie.benefits: Ugh. COB mix-ups happen. Short answer: we need to get both insurers to agree on the coordination order and reprocess the claim. Start with: 1) Confirm subscriber relationships on the service date, 2) collect both EOBs + both member IDs, 3) send a COB correction request to the insurer that paid primary (ask them to re-open and re-adjudicate as secondary/primary as appropriate).

ev an.m: My spouse's HR says they're enrolled as employee + spouse is listed as dependent, but the clinic put the spouse as subscriber at registration. Clinic says they billed what was entered.

sophie.benefits: That's fine — provider error is common. We need two things in parallel: provider refile or provider correction showing correct subscriber, and the insurer that paid primary must accept a COB correction request referencing the other plan. I'll paste a short template for the insurer + a short provider message.

benefits-bot: Note: typical COB reprocessing can take 30-90 days. Mark as "COB correction request". If you get a balance notice, cc benefits immediately to pause collections.

(sophie.benefits): Template for filing with the insurer that paid primary (copy into insurer portal or email):

```
To: [Insurer Provider Relations / Appeals]
Patient: Evan M (DOB: 1989-02-10)
Member ID (primary payer as shown on EOB): SP-5551234
Member ID (Redwood plan): RWD-002345678
Service date: 2026-03-22
Provider claim #: CLM-445566
Amount billed: $760

Issue: The claim was processed with the wrong coordination of benefits. The subscriber on the claim was listed as the spouse; however, the employer coverage hierarchy for the service date is:
- Primary plan: Redwood Inference Benefits (Member: Evan M, Member ID RWD-002345678)
- Secondary plan: Spouse's employer plan (Member: [Spouse Name], Member ID SP-5551234)

Requested action: Please re-open and re-adjudicate the claim using the correct coordination order (Redwood as primary). Attachments: - EOB from the payer showing current adjudication - Copy of Redwood digital ID showing member ID - Copy of spouse's EOB showing their enrollment status (if applicable) - Provider statement indicating billed subscriber

Contact: evan.m@example.com / (555) 555-7777
```

sophie.benefits: Provider message to billing (very short):

```
To: [Clinic Billing]
Patient: Evan M (DOB 1989-02-10)
Service date: 2026-03-22
Original claim ID: CLM-445566

Please void and re-submit the claim with subscriber: Evan M (Member ID RWD-002345678). The original submission billed under [Spouse Name] in error. Please include both member IDs on the corrected claim for COB cross-reference. Email corrected claim/EOB to evan.m@example.com and cc: benefits@redwood.com.
```

linda.hr: Operational: if the spouse's employer needs confirmation that spouse is covered as dependent on your plan (to set coordination), we can provide a benefits verification letter showing dependent status on the service date. That can speed up the carrier's COB processing. DM me the spouse employer contact and I'll draft.

nathan.finance: Finance note: if you end up paying a provider balance because the primary paid incorrectly, hold receipts and the corrected EOBs. Finance can do a provisional reimbursement pending final re-adjudication. Send docs to finance-ops@redwood.com and mark subject "COB provisional reimbursement". Processing time ~2-4 weeks after docs + corrected EOB.

evan.m: Thanks. Quick Q: do insurers accept an employee-submitted appeal or must provider refile?

sophie.benefits: Both paths work. Best practice: ask provider to refile corrected claim (that fixes billing party). Meanwhile, file a COB correction with the insurer that paid primary — attach proof of your Redwood enrollment on service date and the provider statement. If insurer insists provider must refile, have them coordinate; ask insurer to open a provider outreach ticket. We can escalate to our carrier rep if they stall.

benefits-bot: Quick checklist for Evan: 1) Request provider to void/refile with correct subscriber (use provider message above). 2) Upload both EOBs + digital ID + enrollment proof to insurer portal and submit COB correction template. 3) DM @linda.hr provider contact if spouse employer needs a verification letter. 4) If balance posted, cc benefits@redwood.com immediately. 5) Save receipts for finance reimbursement if you pay out-of-pocket.

evan.m: Posting docs now to insurer portal and sending provider message. I'll loop back with any updates. Appreciate the clear templates :thumbsup:
